text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan's foreign trade gap rose to $2.12 billion in July-January compared to $2.09 billion in the year-ago period.
- Nawaz Sharif has called a meeting of industry and business leaders later this month to discuss ways to revamp the economy.
- More than 350 Christians were arrested on Thursday after clashes with police in Karachi.

- Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party candidates, who lost in February 3 polls, have alleged army men inside polling stations were also party to massive rigging as they were seen stamping on Pakistan Muslim League election symbol during polling in many parts of Punjab province.
- Pakistan has denied that any Pakistani organisation was involved in the recent troubles in Xinjiang.
- President Farooq Leghari has summoned the maiden session of the newly elected National Assembly on Saturday.
- The caretaker government announced the National Finance Commission award with provinces getting 37.5 percent of the net proceeds from the divisible pool.
- Pakistan Muslim League secretary general Sartaj Aziz has said the next government would not review agreements with the International Monetary Fund.
